subject: Re: EU<>APAC private deployment — graceful degradation, routing & data handoff
messages:
From: ops@acme.ai (Laura Mills)
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private deployment — routing and data handoff question

Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We need to lock down how traffic will be gracefully degraded across EU and APAC private deployments for our regulated workloads. Two quick asks:  

1) In a partial outage (APAC control plane degraded but compute up), what will traffic routing look like? Specifically: will requests from EU tenants stay in EU, or is there a safety policy that routes to warm-standby in APAC?
2) What evidence can we provide for data residency and KMS key separation for auditors? They want the minimum data movement contracts and artifacts.

We have an urgent security review next Tuesday — can you put together a short technical handoff and checklist?

Laura Mills
Ops Lead, Acme AI
ops@acme.ai


From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: ops@acme.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment — routing and data handoff question

Laura — thanks for the clear asks. Im looping in Hannah (runtime/network), Stephanie (solutions/CS), and Naomi (security) to make sure we cover both operational and compliance needs. Draft plan below and attached is a living checklist (acme-handoff-checklist.xlsx) and a preliminary network diagram (eu-apac-network-diagram.vsdx).

High-level approach (summary):
- Preserve strict data locality by default: EU tenant requests remain in EU region unless explicit cross-region failover is triggered for availability reasons.
- Graceful degradation policy: Prefer in-region warm-standby with prefix/KV cache warming; failover to APAC strict fallback only when regional control plane completely unavailable and customer has accepted degraded residency in contract addendum.
- Routing mechanics: Use per-tenant routing tags + origin enforcement in the edge layer. Route decisions are evaluated at the regional gateway; fallback routes are signed, auditable, and require auto-approval thresholds to be met.
- KMS/key separation: Customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) by default; control plane only holds wrapped keys and provides audit logs. Evidence bundle will include key rotation records, HSM vendor statement, and a signed architecture diagram.

Open questions for team:
- Hannah: details on KV warming / prefix caching strategy during cross-region handoff (TTL expectations, passive vs active sync).
- Naomi: exact evidence set auditors will accept (KMS attestation artifact types, log retention windows).
- Stephanie: update to SOW/contract language that makes residency fallback explicit (we may need a short addendum).

Attachments: acme-handoff-checklist.xlsx, eu-apac-network-diagram.vsdx

Next steps: Can everyone drop notes inline today? Ill consolidate and return a final checklist + DocuSign link by EOD.

— Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment — routing and data handoff question

Karthik / team — quick technical notes (adding inline responses):

> Preserve strict data locality by default: EU tenant requests remain in EU region unless explicit cross-region failover is triggered for availability reasons.
- Agreed. Implementation notes: maintain a tenant-region mapping in the regional gateway service; routing policy must be evaluated downstream of auth so we never proxy EU auth tokens to APAC.

> Graceful degradation policy: Prefer in-region warm-standby with prefix/KV cache warming; failover to APAC strict fallback only when regional control plane completely unavailable and customer has accepted degraded residency in contract addendum.
- KV warm strategy: Use continuous async replication for KV metadata (lightweight) and prefix cache seeding during low traffic windows. Full KV replication for session-critical caches is heavyweight — prefer write-through to origin with read-cache fallback. On failover, we will mark forwarded requests with 'residency-degraded' audit flag.

> Routing mechanics: Use per-tenant routing tags + origin enforcement in the edge layer.
- Edge will advertise two priorities: primary-region and standby-region. Failover is time-gated (configurable threshold, default 5 minutes of control-plane loss) and manual-override available via Console.

> KMS/key separation: Customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) by default; control plane only holds wrapped keys and provides audit logs.
- For on-prem/VPC: we support direct HSM peering (mutual TLS) or envelope encryption model. Need Naomi to confirm minimal artifacts required.

Operational tasks I recommend adding to checklist:
- Warm-cache seeding runbook (owner: runtime-engr)
- Control-plane health signal definitions (owner: infra)
- Audit log retention proof (owner: security)

Ill add these to the checklist and push an updated diagram with sequence flows.

- Hannah
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment — routing and data handoff question

Team — from a security/compliance perspective, key items auditors consistently ask for (Ive listed the minimal acceptable artifacts):

1) KMS separation evidence: customer KMS key IDs, signed HSM vendor attestation (X.509), and KMS access policy snapshots (JSON) showing only customer principals can request unwrapped keys.
2) Data movement contracts: clause references in SOW that state that cross-border data access is only used for explicit availability fallback, and that it will be logged with tenant identifiers. Need traceable DocuSign-backed acceptance from the customer.
3) Audit logs: immutable (append-only) log export for the period requested (default 1 year) and a sample query showing a residency-degraded flag for one failover event.
4) Network evidence: peering / ACL snapshots and BGP/peering tags that show east-west block rules; split the evidence into control-plane and data-plane artifacts.

I attached a stubbed evidence bundle (controlplane-kms-evidence.zip) with placeholder files that show the expected naming and structure for the auditor. Laura — once you confirm specifics for Acme (KMS vendor, retention windows), well swap placeholders for real artifacts.

Questions for Acme:
- Do you require HSM attestation from your KMS vendor, or is a signed vendor letter sufficient?
- Retention window required by auditors (months)?

Naomi
Security Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com

All — great input, thank you. Summary and agreed next steps (for the security review on Tuesday):

Decisions:
- Default model: strict in-region processing. Cross-region fallback is an explicit mode that requires customer's signed addendum.
- Warm-standby approach: prefix/KV cache seeding + time-gated failover (default 5 minutes). Failover events will carry 'residency-degraded' audit markers.
- KMS: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) or HSM peering. We will provide the evidence bundle Naomi described.

Action owners & deadlines:
- Naomi: produce final evidence bundle and example audit export (due: 2027-04-20). Attachment: controlplane-kms-evidence.zip (stubbed).
- Hannah: updated sequence diagram (include cache-seed flow) and warm-cache runbook (due: 2027-04-19).
- Stephanie: draft addendum language for residency fallback and pricing impact (due: 2027-04-19).
- Karthik: consolidate final checklist and send DocuSign link to Acme by 2027-04-19 EOD. Attachment: final-handoff-checklist.pdf

Acme / Laura — please confirm: (1) whether HSM attestation is required, and (2) desired log retention window. Once we have answers Ill route the DocuSign addendum (HS-85219) and the security bundle.

Thanks everyone — well treat this as the canonical thread for the security review.

— Karthik
